solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soak in this way before application

blocks.note: 'so' means in this way, as in 'do it so'
putting something to use is applying it

explanation.surface: Instructions to steep something in a certain manner before applying it, like a fabric treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to drench or steep thoroughly in liquid, a direct synonym of soak.

clue.text: Include subscription amount on end of invoice

indicators.note: 'end of' takes only the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a sub is a short form of subscription
a sum is an amount of money
last letter of invoice

explanation.surface: Adding the membership fee at the bottom of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsume is to absorb something into a larger category, which is to include it.

clue.text: Secretly being very drunk

blocks.note: first meaning: covertly, as of a bribe passed out of sight
second meaning: so drunk as to have slid off one's chair

explanation.surface: Someone hiding how intoxicated they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes covert payments passed beneath a table and also someone collapsed there from drink.

clue.text: Overhear a cause of sagging roof?

definitions.note: a whimsical noun phrase for the verb answer split as a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: listen secretly to others' talk
second meaning, read as two words: a drop in the eaves, the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a drooping roof line.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the word into roof edge plus a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening covertly to a conversation one is not part of is the verb's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Born round disreputable area of London

blocks.note: b. is the standard abbreviation for born
the letter O is round in shape
a rough area or crowd is disreputable

explanation.surface: Someone raised in a seedy part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies the ring-shaped letter. Borough is the district south of London Bridge, home to Borough Market.
explanation.definitionFit: The Borough, or Southwark, is a named district of south London near London Bridge.

clue.text: Bats evidently live flying round … yes, initially here?

definitions.text: Bats evidently live flying round … yes, initially here?

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.clueFragment: Bats evidently live flying round … yes
blocks.note: first letters of the six words

explanation.surface: Pointing to the place bats are known to roost and flutter about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: bats famously live in belfries.
explanation.definitionFit: A belfry is a bell tower, proverbially home to bats, as in 'bats in the belfry'.

clue.text: Tear that's often seen on gravestone

definitions.note: a description rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: ... as a noun, a rent in cloth
second meaning: the abbreviation for Requiescat in pace, rest in peace

explanation.surface: A teardrop shed at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' tempts you towards weeping at a grave, but it rhymes with 'bear' here.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters are both a word for a rent in fabric and the Latin abbreviation carved on tombstones.

clue.text: Republican Ted is running? It's not certain

indicators.note: something running moves about, so these letters are set loose into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Doubt about whether a Republican named Ted is standing for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' suggests standing for election, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpredictable outcome cannot be foreseen, so it is not certain.

clue.text: Run into small building, feel pain

indicators.note: 'into' says one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a hut is a small simple building
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Crashing into a shed and getting injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt as an intransitive verb means to ache or give pain, as in 'my leg hurts'.

clue.text: Plot wicked torment

blocks.note: a garden plot for flowers is a bed
direct synonym

explanation.surface: A villain's scheme to cause suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to harass or plague someone persistently, the same as torment used as a verb.

clue.text: Musician initially performing in support

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for only the opening letter of the word before it
'in' places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a pier is a supporting pillar, as of a bridge
first letter of performing

explanation.surface: A musician who starts out playing as an accompanist.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter sits after the second letter of the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or a pipe, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Boundless disturbance reportedly held sway

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as it is heard said, so the spelling may change

blocks.note: civil disturbance is unrest
a monarch who held sway reigned, which sounds like the weather word

explanation.surface: A sweeping account of upheaval in a kingdom where some power once ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrestrained has no limits or checks on it, so it is boundless.

clue.text: Can origin get sorted out for mineral?

indicators.note: sorting things out means putting them into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a rock's provenance can be established.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerals are non-living matter, not from plants or animals, which is what inorganic describes.

clue.text: Strongly urge sexy shorts must have extremities covered

indicators.note: covering up the extremities hides the outermost letters of each word, leaving only the inside

blocks.note: sexy without its first and last letters
shorts without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A prim instruction that revealing shorts must cover the wearer's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'extremities' are limbs; cryptically they are the end letters of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge someone earnestly and forcefully to do something.

clue.text: Some signs unknown company holds help back

indicators.note: 'holds' means one piece grips the other inside it
'back' tells us to read that combined part from right to left

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
Co. is the abbreviation for company
direct synonym

explanation.surface: A firm of unknown name turning down a request for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The company abbreviation wraps the help word, and that whole unit is then turned round after the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the belt of twelve astrological signs, so it is a set of signs.

clue.text: Bob has lorry mostly climbing? Yes, climbing

indicators.note: 'mostly' means all but the final letter is kept
in a down answer, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a truck is the American name for a lorry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Bob owns a lorry that labours uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, but it is the quick dip of a curtsey. 'climbing' appears twice, reversing each part separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick bending movement, the short curtsey a woman makes in greeting.

clue.text: Notes on scriptures used in Christmas oratorio

indicators.note: 'used in' means the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Annotations on sacred texts appearing in a seasonal choral work, such as Bach's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masora is the body of traditional Jewish notes on the text of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Barking pet guards the family member

indicators.note: 'barking' means mad, and mad letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, used together

explanation.surface: A noisy dog protecting one of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the noise the pet makes, but it is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepdaughter is a spouse's daughter from an earlier relationship, so a member of the family.

clue.text: Against upsetting no-good giant?

indicators.note: 'no-good' asks us to drop the letter standing for good
upsetting things knocks them out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to toppling a villainous giant.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the standard abbreviation for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning opposed to, the same as against.

clue.text: Former gold coin of imposing appearance

blocks.note: first meaning: an old English gold coin first struck under Edward III
second meaning: stately, grand-looking

explanation.surface: A grand old gold coin admired by a collector.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble was a medieval English gold coin worth a third of a pound; as an adjective the word also means grand or stately.

clue.text: Consume natural fuel when short of power

indicators.note: 'short of' means lacking, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: peat is dug from bogs and burnt as fuel
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Burning a natural fuel during a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consume' fits the fuel story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to consume it.

clue.text: Westwards advance in second vehicle

indicators.note: in an across answer, travelling west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
taken as written
a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: An army pushing west within moments, perhaps by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is used literally. Sub is British informal for an advance on one's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full old name for a bus, a public road vehicle.

clue.text: Unfortunately I retain a tendency not to change

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters go awry

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone admitting regretfully that they are stuck in their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the physical property of resisting changes in motion, and figuratively a reluctance to act.

clue.text: Cold cut, ultimately very tough

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points to the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: C marks the cold tap
to hew is to cut with an axe
last letter of very

explanation.surface: A chilled slice of meat that turns out very hard to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy food takes a lot of chewing, as tough meat does.
